newsitem.title: ITALY: UN agency urges better pesticide control in Africa.
newsitem.headline: UN agency urges better pesticide control in Africa.

text.p: The U.N.'s Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) called on Thursday for tighter controls on the use and trade of toxic pesticides and chemicals in Africa.
The Rome-based agency issued a statement to coincide with a meeting of officials from 100 governments in Nairobi for talks to prepare an international treaty on hazardous chemicals.
FAO said organo-chlorine pesticides, such as DDT, which have been banned or whose use has been severely restricted in Europe and North America, are still marketed and used in Africa.
Some African states have no approved pesticides legislation.
Niek Van der Graaf, chief of FAO's plant protection service, said that poverty, instability and unreliable rains meant that pesticide use in Africa was lowest overall of all continents.
But he added, "There are areas of intensive pesticide use... for example by large-scale commercial farms, vegetable production around cities and plantations producing export crops".

FAO says a better-applied Prior Informed Consent procedure, which lets countries know about toxic substances that may be shipped to them allowing them to choose to permit or ban future imports, would help reduce health and environmental risks.

"Considerable scope remains for technical assistance to improve pesticide regulations and pesticide management," Van der Graaf said. "Restrictions on products that cannot be handled safely in developing countries should be considered by the industry and governments."
